acceptance: The stable package exports closed v1 privacy vocabularies plus the processing-purpose list field, without framework, model-provider, or database coupling.
Deterministic node validation rejects any value outside a declared privacy vocabulary with DOMAIN_INVALID_ENUM_VALUE, and unknown privacy attributes keep failing closed.

Deterministic governance validation reports consent without user-visible state, an audit or minimization requirement without a redaction control, and public visibility of data that requires a handling policy, each with a stable error code and no false positive on the documented negative cases.
Issue collection remains total and deterministic across repeated runs, node and edge insertion orders, and JSON object key orders, under the documented phase order and sort key.
Domain validation does not mutate, reorder, or normalize its input, and well-formed Product Graph v1 canonical revision identity is unchanged by domain validation.
Focused privacy tests plus the full repository format, lint, typecheck, and test suites pass on the exact candidate, and Ubuntu and Windows CI both pass.
Diffcipline exact-candidate proof, Alibaba OCR deterministic accounting/rule resolution with semantic review, and Jev typed judgments are recorded before guarded merge.

required: Stable @ineractive/product-graph privacy vocabularies, processing-purpose field, and the three deterministic governance privacy rules with focused tests.
Proof that out-of-vocabulary privacy input fails closed and that canonical revision identity is unchanged for well-formed documents.
Exact-candidate Diffcipline proof, Alibaba OCR deterministic accounting/rule resolution with semantic review, and Jev typed judgments.
Exact-head Ubuntu and Windows repository CI plus post-merge fresh-main qualification.

minimality.rationale: Extend the already-qualified stable package with one bounded set of privacy vocabularies and three governance rules plus focused tests, instead of adding a package, promoting the prototype lab, or introducing a runtime dependency.

requirements: Privacy validation composes on top of the node, edge, relation, and governance layers delivered by SG-000020 through SG-000023 and the Product Graph v1 core contract, and must never weaken or bypass any of them.
Deterministic validation must not depend on object iteration accidents, wall-clock time, randomness, network calls, or model inference.

Declaring consent, visibility, redaction, minimization, or a processing purpose must never be presented as legal or regulatory compliance, and no validator may claim compliance or encode jurisdiction-specific rules.

outcome: The stable @ineractive/product-graph domain layer declares closed v1 privacy vocabularies for collection source, user visibility, consent, redaction, and minimization on the datapolicy node kind, adds a free-form processing-purpose list, and extends the governance phase with deterministic rules that report consent without user-visible state, an audit or minimization requirement without a redaction control, and public visibility of data that requires a handling policy.
rationale: SG-000023 delivered the data-governance relations and cross-node rules of IN-P02-S02-T02 and deferred the privacy semantics to this dependent Grain; the canonical DataPolicy definition names consent, redaction, and user-visible preference state as required semantics.

risk.recovery: Revert the SG-000024 privacy vocabularies, the processing-purpose field, the enum registrations, the three governance privacy rules, the focused tests, the evidence record, and the current-frontier update; the SG-000022 and SG-000023 classification, lifecycle, relation, and governance layers, the earlier domain layer, the Product Graph v1 contracts, and ADR-0003 remain intact and no production state is mutated.

scope_in: Declare closed v1 privacy vocabularies for the datapolicy node kind: collection source, user visibility, consent, redaction, and minimization, in the same data-driven vocabulary style as the SG-000022 classification and lifecycle fields.

Declare the optional processing-purpose list field on the datapolicy node kind as a free-form string list, because processing purposes are product-specific and a closed vocabulary would invent business meaning.
Register the new privacy attributes in the enum field table so an out-of-vocabulary value is reported as the stable node-phase error code DOMAIN_INVALID_ENUM_VALUE.
Extend the governance phase with the stable error code DOMAIN_CONSENT_WITHOUT_USER_VISIBILITY for a policy that requires consent while its own visibility is not user-visible.
Extend the governance phase with the stable error code DOMAIN_MISSING_REDACTION_CONTROL for a policy that requires audit or minimization while declaring no redaction control.

Extend the governance phase with the stable error code DOMAIN_PUBLIC_VISIBILITY_OF_CLASSIFIED_DATA for a policy that declares public visibility while governing data classified at a level that requires a handling policy.

Add focused deterministic tests covering every new vocabulary value, every new enum field, out-of-vocabulary privacy values, each new rule with its negative cases, deterministic ordering, no input mutation, and unchanged canonical revision identity.
Advance specs/CURRENT.md to record SG-000023 canonical closure and SG-000024 as the active frontier Grain.
scope_out: No new node or edge kinds, no change to the classification or lifecycle vocabularies, and no change to any relation or endpoint pair delivered by earlier Grains.
No locale, external-effect, Dataset, design-system, skill, exploration-branch, or release semantics.
No Change Intent, proposed graph delta, Question Gate, Assumption Ledger, graph views, compiler, database, Supabase migration, or remote side effect.
No claim of legal or regulatory compliance, no regulatory taxonomy, and no jurisdiction-specific rule.
No new workspace package, no new runtime dependency, no lockfile change, and no relaxation of existing rejection behavior.
title: IN-P02-S02-T02C Implement privacy semantics
